text:
Eli (support): Hey team — urgent customer escalation from ACME (prod) after our scheduled KMS rotation. Their API calls to /v1/private/decrypt are returning 403s. Logs show AccessDeniedException mentioning encryption context mismatch. Customer can't decrypt tokens. Can we triage?

SecurityBot: Automated job: rotated CMK alias/ci-prod-enc -> key/abcd-rotated at 2026-11-03T21:12:00Z by arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/kms-rotator. No immediate errors on rotation job.

Maya (sec-eng): Copy the exact error and paste the CloudTrail Decrypt event if you have it. Also confirm whether they use cross-account roles or grants (grants are common for service accounts).

Eli (support): Error from app logs: "com.amazonaws.services.kms.model.AccessDeniedException: The request was denied because the encryption context did not match the one used to encrypt the ciphertext."
CloudTrail Decrypt requestParameters snippet: 
{
  "ciphertextBlob": "<redacted>",
  "encryptionContext": {"purpose":"redwood-cache", "release":"2026-10-31"},
  "keyId": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444444:key/abcd-rotated"
}

Tom (infra): Common causes: 1) ciphertext was encrypted with different encryptionContext (even a small key/value change breaks decrypt). 2) Decrypt principal lacks kms:Decrypt for this key or has a Condition that doesn't match. 3) The rotation script re-wrapped ciphertext with a different context.

Tom (infra): Quick repro steps for us to try locally:
```bash
# fetch ciphertext (from example)
aws s3 cp s3://acme-prod-secrets/ct.bin ./ct.bin
# try decrypt with explicit context
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context purpose=redwood-cache,release=2026-10-31 --region us-west-2 --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444444:key/abcd-rotated --output json
```
If that fails, try listing the encryptionContext stored in CloudTrail and compare exact key order/spacing.

Maya (sec-eng): Also check whether their KMS key policy or IAM policy uses condition keys referencing the encryption context. Example failing policy snippet we saw before: 
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowDecryptWithExactContext",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444444:role/service-role" },
  "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {
      "kms:EncryptionContext:release": "2026-10-30"
    }
  }
}
```
If the rotation bumped "release" to 2026-10-31 in encryptionContext, that policy would now deny. Ask the customer whether any code path changed the context values during rotation.

Eli (support): They confirmed the rotation automation updated the "release" value in their deploy pipeline to match the new release tag. That likely caused the mismatch — but earlier ciphertexts were produced with "release": "2026-10-30".

Maya (sec-eng): Two remediation approaches:
1) Short-term: allow decryption by relaxing the Condition temporarily (e.g., remove the kms:EncryptionContext:release equality OR allow a set of acceptable values) so legacy ciphertexts can decrypt. Update key policy/IAM policy accordingly then revert after rewrap.
2) Proper: re-encrypt (rewrap) all ciphertexts with the new context using kms:ReEncrypt or decrypt+encrypt server-side with correct contexts. This preserves least privilege.

Tom (infra): Rewrap example (AWS CLI):
```bash
# re-encrypt from old ciphertext to new key/context
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin \
  --source-encryption-context release=2026-10-30,purpose=redwood-cache \
  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444444:key/abcd-rotated \
  --destination-encryption-context release=2026-10-31,purpose=redwood-cache \
  --region us-west-2 \
  --output json > ct_rewrapped.json
```
If the customer has many objects, run a batch job on a worker fleet.

Maya (sec-eng): Also double-check grants: if the service relied on KMS grants (CreateGrant) to permit a cross-account role, grants are tied to CMK and might not survive alias-level swaps if the rotation created a brand new key and the grant wasn't recreated. Use \`aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>\`.

Eli (support): Customer says they used alias swap (alias -> new-key) during rotation and did not recreate grants. That could explain AccessDenied for principals that relied on grant tokens.

Oncall (eng-sre): Short mitigation options we can help the customer with: 1) Recreate grants for the new key pointing to the service principal. 2) Re-encrypt objects via re-encrypt tool. 3) Temporarily relax policy conditions while rewrap runs. I'll open a runbook for the re-encrypt job and coordinate capacity.

Maya (sec-eng): Policy to allow decrypt for multiple releases (example):
```json
"Condition": {
  "StringLike": {
    "kms:EncryptionContext:release": ["2026-10-30", "2026-10-31"]
  }
}
```
But be careful: expanding allowed values increases blast radius. Make sure to revert after re-encrypt.

Eli (support): I'll propose the temporary policy change and the re-encrypt plan to ACME. They asked for exact steps to re-create grants. Can we provide a minimal grant create example?

Tom (infra): Grant example:
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444444:key/abcd-rotated \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::555555:role/service-role \
  --operations Decrypt,Encrypt,ReEncryptFrom,ReEncryptTo,GenerateDataKey --name "acme-service-grant"
```
Remember to persist the GrantId returned and audit with CloudTrail.

Maya (sec-eng): Also ask ACME to send the CloudTrail Decrypt event with "encryptionContext" for both successful (pre-rotation) and failing (post-rotation) calls; that will prove context drift.

Eli (support): Got it. I'll request: 1) sample CloudTrail Decrypt events, 2) current key policy/IAM policy, 3) whether they used grants and any grant IDs, 4) confirmation of alias swap vs rewrap.

Oncall (eng-sre): I'll standby to run a temporary policy patch if they approve. If they opt for re-encrypt, I'll schedule the job during off-peak and post timing here. :thumbsup:

Maya (sec-eng): Also note for future rotations: automation should preserve encryptionContext for existing data or perform in-place rewrap as part of rotation workflow. We'll draft a rotation hardened checklist.

Eli (support): Thanks — escalating to account team now. Will update with CloudTrail snippets when they arrive.
